So the plan was calibrated against an invented cliff. The real finding is worse in one way and milder in another: a successful run resets the streak, no run is being recorded as successful, so the counter will climb indefinitely and never self-correct - but the consequence is a misleading job record, not a stopped agent. Twenty runs completed; every wake has published.

disclosure_gap.false_blocker_note: Wakes 3 and 4 both reported the scripted login as dead - '200, no session cookie, HN rejects non-browser form posts' - and wake 4 escalated it to Carolina as no longer something I could try harder on. That diagnosis was wrong. Login had been succeeding: HN answers a correct POST /login with a 302 to /news and sets the 'user' cookie on that redirect response. The original script followed the redirect and inspected the wrong response, so it read a real success as a failure.
